headline: OpenAI drops NDAs for data centers
dek: The end of secrecy with officials follows the election, per CNBC.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: End of secrecy
body: OpenAI said it will stop using non-disclosure agreements with public officials on data centers it owns and operates, per CNBC Technology, SiliconANGLE and The Verge AI.
It will seek only narrow protections for security, trade secrets or sensitive data.

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: New commitments
s3.body: Per SiliconANGLE and The Verge AI:

points.t: Will publish construction plans and noise projections.
Will disclose the jobs each data center should create.
Each project gets a contact to answer residents.

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Election backlash
body: The news came two days after the election, where voters rejected data centers in most local votes, per CNBC Technology.
OpenAI reaffirmed it pays the full cost of power and grid upgrades.

stat.cap: local measures went against, per CNBC

items.t: OpenAI urges lawmakers to make this law (CNBC Technology).
Meta, Microsoft, Google and Anthropic made similar pledges (CNBC Technology).
Will cut power draw at peak demand (SiliconANGLE).

caption.hook: OpenAI says it will stop using NDAs with public officials at its data centers.
body: Per CNBC, SiliconANGLE and The Verge, the company will seek only narrow protections for security information, trade secrets or sensitive data. The news came two days after the US election, where voters rejected data centers in most local votes.

OpenAI will also publish construction plans and noise projections, disclose expected jobs and create a local compact for each project, with a contact for residents. It reaffirmed it pays the full cost of power and grid upgrades and urged lawmakers to turn these practices into law for the whole industry.
caption.cta: Should every data center drop its NDAs?
